notes: Ten web searches ran, all listed in 'searches'; none were refused. The required searches on general AI, superintelligence and 'AI safety', extinction or existential risk, pause or moratorium (including data centers), China agreement, and her campaign site all ran; the site-restricted search returned no pages from marypeltola.com, so I opened her home page and story page directly (neither mentions AI; the site has no issues page). She was not in Congress during 2025-2026 (House term ended January 2025; Senate term not yet begun), so she could not have signed the 23 September 2026 letter on AI talks with China (not on the verified signer list) or co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act; I found no source showing she commented on either. Paraphrases left out: (1) Newsweek (page undated; correction note 21 Oct 2026) says 'Peltola has centered her campaign on affordability and energy costs generally rather than data centers specifically' - reporter's words, not hers. (2) Alaska Beacon (3 Nov 2026 per search summary; page could not be opened, HTTP 403, also via newsfromthestates.com) reports that she received at least $56,000 from AI-company employees, nearly all from Anthropic employees, and, per the search summary, that neither campaign responded to requests for comment; this is campaign money, not a statement, and is unverified at source. (3) An NRSC ad against her was partly made with AI (search summary of Washington Examiner / NRSC); her campaign called it misleading per the summary; not about AI risk and not read at source. Not checked: her X account (out of scope), debate transcripts (no search hit linking AI to the Peltola-Sullivan debates), her 2025 statements as a private citizen beyond what the searches returned, and her final House months (before 1 January 2025, out of scope anyway). Name check: many search hits were unrelated Finnish people surnamed Peltola, and a different 'Dan J. Sullivan' (alleged spoiler candidate) appears in coverage; none of these were used.
